en.title: Slovenia: snow line holds at 2,000 m as early flakes begin
en.description: Early November snow covers 1,130 km2 of Slovenia. The ground turns white above 2,000 m elevation; below that, most slopes stay brown. Data from 16 November 2026.
en.lede: Snow in Slovenia sits cleanly at one elevation boundary: above 2,000 m the mountains are mostly white, below that they are mostly bare. After a week of steady gain, the snow cover stopped growing yesterday, though a significant system arrives Thursday.

p: Walk up the Slovenian mountains and you hit a sharp transition. Below 2,000 m, only patchy white touches the ground—even at 1,500 m to 2,000 m, where you might expect continuous cover, only 35 percent of the slope shows snow. The air is still warm enough to melt what falls. Cross that 2,000 m line and the picture flips: 74 percent of the terrain is snow-covered, with an average depth of 6 cm according to our model.

This is where you find the best skiing right now. The Julian Alps, the highest peaks in the country, have picked up 3 cm in the past three days. At lower elevations—1,000 m to 1,500 m—the snow is thin and fragile, often just 1 cm on average. Even that disappears fast when the sun strengthens. The highest resorts, like Vogel at 1,731 m, have enough base to stay skiable, but the low-altitude areas are racing against autumn warmth.

Breaking it down by height bands, the story is clear. At 500 m to 1,000 m—the foothills—just 12 percent of the land is white and the average depth is 1 cm. That is not useful snow. Jump to 1,000 m to 1,500 m and you get 17 percent coverage with the same thin 1 cm average.

At 1,500 m to 2,000 m you see the transition zone: coverage rises to 35 percent and depth to 2 cm. Then, above 2,000 m, the air is cold enough to preserve what falls. That is where 74 percent of the ground is covered and depths reach 6 cm. If you plan to ski this week, stay high.

sections.h: Overall area: a week of rapid gain
p: One week ago, only 220 km2 of Slovenia was white. Today, 1,130 km2 is snow-covered. That is a jump of 910 km2 in seven days—a dramatic shift from bare slopes to a partly snow-dressed country. Yesterday the coverage shrank by 80 km2, the first pullback after steady accumulation, likely due to daytime melt on south-facing slopes below 2,000 m.

In total, 15 of the 27 Slovenian ski resorts now have measurable snow on the ground. That is half the network, and all those resorts sit above 1,000 m where yesterday's loss was modest. The white share across the whole modelled area is 15 percent—low by winter standards, but high for mid-November.

Gače, the low-altitude resort at 964 m, still holds the deepest pack: 28 cm measured at the station on 16 November. That is well above normal for this date and shows how much fresh snow fell here early in the week. Vogel, the Alpine resort at 1,731 m, sits close behind with 26 cm and has picked up 1 cm in the past three days. Velika planina at 1,664 m has 24 cm.

Below that tier, Rogla and Golte—both above 1,500 m—have thinner bases of 17 cm and 16 cm respectively, and they have not gained snow in the past three days. The difference is height and exposure. The highest peaks continue to accumulate; the mid-altitude resorts are losing mass to melt. By next week, the balance may shift as fresh powder falls onto the high ridges.

Thursday 19 November is the trigger date. Our model predicts 6 cm of new snow that day—the heaviest single day in the coming week. If that forecast holds, the snowiest day of the next seven days will be 19 November, and the total for the next week could reach 7 cm. That fresh powder will land on existing bases and should deepen the snow above 2,000 m significantly.
The following week, 24 to 30 November, looks even richer: up to 33 cm is forecast. That is when the winter pattern really begins to take shape. For now, Thursday's storm is the event to watch.

Compared to past Novembers, this is good timing. At Gače, the typical depth in mid-November is zero; today it is 3 cm by the same measure. At Vogel, the usual depth equals what we see now. Five of the five major resorts tracked are running above their November average, and four of them are above normal by a margin.

Nearby Austria is running much deeper—Austria's leader, Kaprun, has 83 cm and faces 50 cm more snow in the next week. Italy's Monterosa Ski holds 99 cm. Slovenia is behind that tier, but the trajectory is clear. Use this week to ski high. By late November, the low resorts may become viable again as the snow deepens.

advice: Stay above 2,000 m this week. That is where 74 percent of the ground is white and depths reach 6 cm. Lower elevations are patchy and thinning daily due to melt.
Expect the best skiing on 19 November after the main snow pulse arrives. Fresh powder will collect most heavily on the high ridges and summits.
Watch for thin snow cover over rock and ice below 1,500 m. Even 1 cm average depth means many runs are still brown or exposed. Test terrain carefully.
By late November, the second storm system (24–30 November) may make lower resorts viable. If you are flexible, consider waiting a few days rather than skiing now on bare slopes.
Check the official avalanche bulletin for the Julian Alps and high peaks before going off-piste, especially after Thursday's new snow.

captions.map: Snow-covered area of Slovenia on 16 November 2026, showing 1,130 km2 white. The snow line sits at 2,000 m elevation, with heavy cover in the high peaks and patchy cover below 1,500 m.

sl.title: Slovenija: snežna meja na 2.000 m, prve plahute snega se pojavljajo
sl.description: Zgodnji novembrski sneg pokriva 1.130 km2 Slovenije. Tla se belijo nad 2.000 m; spodaj ostajajo pobočja smeđa. Podatki od 16. novembra 2026.
sl.lede: Sneg v Sloveniji leži čisto na eni nadmorski višini: nad 2.000 m so gore večinoma bele, spodaj pa so večinoma gole. Po tednu stalnega naraščanja se je snežna odeja včeraj ustavila, čeprav bo v četrtek prišlo do pomembnega vremena.

p: Ko se povzpnete po slovenskih gorah, naletite na oster prehod. Pod 2.000 m se sneg dotika tla le tu in tam—tudi med 1.500 m in 2.000 m, kjer bi pričakovali neprekinjeno pokritost, je snežna le le 35 odstotkov pobočja. Zrak je še vedno dovolj topel, da stopi, kar pada. Ko prečkate 2.000 m mejo, se slika obrne: 74 odstotkov terena je pokrito s snegom, povprečna globina pa je 6 cm po našem modelu.

Tu je trenutno najboljša smuka. Julijskie Alpe, najvišji vrhovi v državi, so v zadnjih treh dneh nabirале 3 cm. Na nižjih nadmorskih višinah—1.000 m do 1.500 m—je sneg tanek in krhek, v povprečju le 1 cm. Tudi ta hitro izgine, ko se sonce ojača. Največji resorti, kot je Vogel na 1.731 m, imajo dovolj podlage za smuko, toda področja na nižjih nadmorskih višinah tekmujejo s jesensko toploto.

Razdeliti po pasu nadmorske višine je zgodba jasna. Na 500 m do 1.000 m—u predgorjih—je le 12 odstotkov zemlje bele in povprečna globina je 1 cm. To ni uporaben sneg. Skočite na 1.000 m do 1.500 m in dobite 17 odstotkov pokritosti z isto tankima 1 cm povprečje.

Med 1.500 m in 2.000 m vidite prehodnico: pokritost naraste na 35 odstotkov in globina na 2 cm. Potem, nad 2.000 m, je zrak dovolj mrzel, da ohranja, kar pada. Tu je 74 odstotkov tal pokritih in globine dosegajo 6 cm. Če načrtujete smuko to sredo, ostanite visoko.

Pred tednom je le 220 km2 Slovenije bilo bele barve. Danes je 1.130 km2 prekritih s snegom. To je preskok 910 km2 v sedmih dneh—dramatičen premik z golih pobočij na delno sneženo državo. Včeraj se je pokritost zmanjšala za 80 km2, prvi umik po stalnem nabiranju, verjetno zaradi dnevnega taljenja na južno obrnjenihpobočjih pod 2.000 m.

Skupno ima 15 od 27 slovenskih smučarskih resorjev zdaj merljiv sneg na tleh. To je polovica mreže in vsi ti resorti se nahajajo nad 1.000 m, kjer je bil včerajšnji upad skromen. Beli delež čez celotno modelirano področje je 15 odstotkov—nizko po zimskih standardih, toda visoko za sredino novembra.

Gače, resort na nizki nadmorski višini 964 m, ima še vedno najglobljo podlago: 28 cm izmerjeno na postaji 16. novembra. To je dobro nad povprečjem za ta datum in kaže, koliko svežega snega je padlo tu zgodaj v tednu. Vogel, alpski resort na 1.731 m, zaostaja tik za tem z 26 cm in je nabiral 1 cm v zadnjih treh dneh. Velika planina na 1.664 m ima 24 cm.

Pod to stopnjo sta Rogla in Golte—oba nad 1.500 m—s tanjšimi podlagami 17 cm in 16 cm, narazen, in nista nabirala snega v zadnjih treh dneh. Razlika je višina in izpostavljenost. Najvišji vrhovi se še vedno nabirajo; resorti na srednji nadmorski višini izgubljajo maso zaradi taljenja. Prihodnji teden se bo ravnovesje morda spremenilo, ko bo sveža prah padla na visoke slemenove.

Četrtek 19. november je ključni datum. Naš model napoveduje 6 cm novega snega ta dan—najtežji posamezni dan v prihodnje tednu. Če ta napoved držim, bo najbolj snežen dan prihodnjega tedna 19. november, skupno za prihodnji teden pa bi lahko doseglo 7 cm. Ta svež prah bo padel na obstoječe podlage in bi moral bistveno poglobiti sneg nad 2.000 m.

Naslednji teden, 24. do 30. novembra, je videti še bogatejši: napovedanih je do 33 cm. To je takrat, ko se zimski vzorec res začne oblikovati. Zaenkrat je četrtkova nevihta dogodek, ki ga je treba opazovati.

V primerjavi s prejšnjimi novembri je to dobro čašovanje. Pri Gačah je običajna globina v sredini novembra nič; danes je 3 cm po isti meritvi. Pri Voglu je običajna globina enaka temu, kar vidimo zdaj. Pet od petih glavnih resorjev, ki jih sledimo, teče nad svojim novembrskim povprečjem, štiri od njih pa so nad povprečjem za razliko.

Sosednja Avstrija je tekla precej globlje—Avstrijski vodilni Kaprun ima 83 cm in mu sledi 50 cm več snega v naslednjem tednu. Italijanska Monterosa Ski drži 99 cm. Slovenija je za to stopnjo, toda trajektorija je jasna. To sredo ostanite visoko. Do konca novembra bi resorti na nižjih nadmorskih višinah morda postali spet uporabni, ko se sneg poglobi.

advice: Ostanite nad 2.000 m to sredo. Tu je 74 odstotkov tal belo in globine dosegajo 6 cm. Nižje nadmorske višine so madežne in se tanjšajo dnevno zaradi taljenja.
Pričakujte najboljšo smuko 19. novembra po prihodu glavnega snežnega pulza. Svež prah se bo nabieral največje na visokih slemenih in vrhovih.
Bodite pozorni na tanko snežno pokritost nad skalo in ledom pod 1.500 m. Tudi povprečje 1 cm pomeni, da je veliko proge še vedno smeđe ali odprto. Progo testirajte previdno.
Do konca novembra bo drugi vremenska sistem (24.–30. november) morda naredil nižje resorte uporabne. Če ste prožni, razmislite, da počakate nekaj dni namesto smuke zdaj po golih pobočjih.
Preden greste s terensko smuko, preverite uraden plaz bulletin za Julijskie Alpe in visoke vrhove, še posebej po četrkovi sveži snegi.

captions.map: Snežna površina Slovenije 16. novembra 2026, kar kaže 1.130 km2 bele barve. Snežna meja se nahaja na 2.000 m nadmorske višine, s težko pokritostjo v visokih vrhovih in madežno pokritostjo pod 1.500 m.
